name: Learn: Resource Quotas & Limit Ranges
objective: CKAD › Application Environment, Configuration and Security. Drill EVERY corner of namespace resource governance harder than the exam: compute ResourceQuota, object-count quota, scoped quota (BestEffort), LimitRange defaults, LimitRange min/max bounds, ratio limits, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix of a pod rejected by a quota. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Eight strict governance practicals in one namespace. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: ResourceQuota — cap total compute
questions.teach:
A **ResourceQuota** caps a namespace's totals. A *compute* quota tracks `requests.cpu`, `requests.memory`, `limits.cpu`, `limits.memory`. Create it with `kubectl create quota <name> --hard=... -n <ns>`.

**Gotcha:** the four keys use dots (`requests.cpu`) — in jsonpath you must escape them (`spec.hard.requests\.cpu`).
questions.prompt:
In namespace `ckad-quotas`, create a ResourceQuota named `compute-quota` with hard limits: `requests.cpu=1`, `requests.memory=1Gi`, `limits.cpu=2`, `limits.memory=2Gi`.

Target: `compute-quota` shows exactly those four hard values.

verification.description: compute-quota has the four compute hard limits (1/1Gi/2/2Gi)

questions.title: A pod that fits under the compute quota
questions.teach:
Once a compute quota tracks a resource, **every new pod must declare both requests AND limits** for that resource or admission rejects it. Give the container a `resources:` block with values that fit under the quota.

**Gotcha:** omit even one dimension (e.g. `limits.memory`) and the pod is rejected with `must specify limits.memory`.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-quotas`, create pod `fits` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`, container name `app`) with `requests` cpu `200m` / memory `256Mi` and `limits` cpu `500m` / memory `512Mi`. It must be admitted and reach Running.

Target: pod `fits` is Running and declares exactly those requests and limits.
questions.hint: Write YAML with a full `resources` block (both requests and limits, all four values) and apply it.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: fits, namespace: ckad-quotas }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    resources:
      requests: { cpu: 200m, memory: 256Mi }
      limits: { cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi }
YAML

verification.description: pod 'fits' is Running with exact requests 200m/256Mi + limits 500m/512Mi

questions.title: ResourceQuota — cap object counts
questions.teach:
A ResourceQuota can also cap the **number of objects**. Built-in count names include `pods`, `services`, `secrets`, `configmaps`; a generic form is `count/<resource>.<group>` (e.g. `count/deployments.apps`). `--hard=configmaps=3` allows at most three.

**Gotcha:** counts are **current live objects**, not cumulative — delete an object and the slot frees up.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-quotas`, create a ResourceQuota named `object-quota` with hard counts: `configmaps=3` and `count/deployments.apps=2`.

Target: `object-quota` has hard `configmaps: 3` and `count/deployments.apps: 2`.

questions.title: Scoped ResourceQuota (BestEffort)
questions.teach:
A quota can apply **only to a subset of pods** via `scopes`. `BestEffort` matches pods with NO resource requests/limits; `NotBestEffort`, `Terminating`, `NotTerminating` are the others. `kubectl create quota ... --scopes=BestEffort`.

**Gotcha:** a `BestEffort` quota may only set `pods` (count) — it can't cap cpu/memory, since BestEffort pods have none.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-quotas`, create a ResourceQuota named `be-quota` scoped to `BestEffort`, with hard `pods=1`.

Target: `be-quota` has hard `pods: 1` and `spec.scopes` contains `BestEffort`.

verification.description: be-quota: hard pods=1 scoped to BestEffort

questions.title: LimitRange — default requests & limits
questions.teach:
A **LimitRange** (type `Container`) injects resources into pods that omit them: `defaultRequest` supplies the **requests**, `default` supplies the **limits**. This is what lets a bare pod satisfy a compute quota. **Gotcha:** defaults are injected at admission — verify on the pod (`kubectl get pod

-o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].resources}'`), never from your YAML.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-quotas`, create a LimitRange `defaults` (type `Container`) with `defaultRequest` cpu `200m` / memory `128Mi` and `default` (limits) cpu `500m` / memory `256Mi`. Then create pod `nodefaults` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`, container name `app`) with **no** resources block.

Target: pod `nodefaults`'s container ends up with requests cpu `200m` / memory `128Mi` and limits cpu `500m` / memory `256Mi`.
questions.hint: Apply the LimitRange (type Container, default + defaultRequest) FIRST, then `kubectl -n ckad-quotas run nodefaults --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600`; check with jsonpath on `.spec.containers[0].resources`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata: { name: defaults, namespace: ckad-quotas }
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    defaultRequest: { cpu: 200m, memory: 128Mi }
    default: { cpu: 500m, memory: 256Mi }
YAML
kubectl -n ckad-quotas run nodefaults --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600

verification.description: nodefaults inherited requests 200m/128Mi + limits 500m/256Mi from the LimitRange

questions.title: LimitRange — min and max bounds
questions.teach:
A LimitRange (type `Container`) also enforces **per-container bounds**: `min` is the floor and `max` the ceiling. A container requesting below `min` or limiting above `max` is rejected at admission.

**Gotcha:** a bare integer `cpu: 1` in YAML is read as a number — quote it (`cpu: "1"`) so it round-trips as the string `1`.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-quotas`, create a LimitRange `constraints` (type `Container`) with `min` cpu `100m` / memory `64Mi` and `max` cpu `1` / memory `1Gi`.

Target: `constraints` has min cpu `100m`, min memory `64Mi`, max cpu `1`, max memory `1Gi`.
questions.hint: Apply a LimitRange YAML with `type: Container`, `min: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}`, `max: {cpu: "1", memory: 1Gi}`.

verification.description: constraints LimitRange: min cpu 100m/mem 64Mi, max cpu 1/mem 1Gi

questions.title: LimitRange — maxLimitRequestRatio
questions.teach:
`maxLimitRequestRatio` on a LimitRange caps how far a container's **limit** may exceed its **request** per resource. `cpu: 4` means `limit/request` must be ≤ 4 — a container requesting `100m` can't limit above `400m`.

**Gotcha:** the ratio constrains the gap, not absolute values — it's independent of `min`/`max`, and a pod violating it is rejected at admission.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-quotas`, create a LimitRange `ratios` (type `Container`) with `maxLimitRequestRatio` cpu `4`.

Target: `ratios` has `spec.limits[0].maxLimitRequestRatio.cpu` = `4`.
questions.hint: Apply a LimitRange YAML: `type: Container`, `maxLimitRequestRatio: {cpu: "4"}` (quote it so it round-trips as a string).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata: { name: ratios, namespace: ckad-quotas }
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    maxLimitRequestRatio: { cpu: "4" }
YAML

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a pod rejected by the quota
questions.teach:
When a compute quota exists, a pod whose container omits a tracked dimension is **refused at admission** — so a Deployment's pod never gets created and it stays `0/1`. `kubectl -n <ns> get replicaset` / `describe rs` surfaces the error `must specify limits.cpu` (or similar).

**Gotcha:** fix the **Deployment's pod template** to declare the missing requests/limits — don't touch the quota.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `shipit` in `ckad-quotas` is stuck at `0/1` — its pods are **rejected by `compute-quota`** because the container doesn't declare all required resources. Diagnose the rejection and fix the Deployment's pod template so a pod is admitted and the Deployment reports an available replica. Don't change the quota; don't delete and rebuild.

Target: Deployment `shipit` has at least 1 available replica.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n ckad-quotas describe rs -l app=shipit` → `failed quota: ... must specify limits.cpu,limits.memory,requests.cpu,requests.memory`. Edit the Deployment to add a full `resources` block (e.g. requests 100m/64Mi, limits 200m/128Mi), then watch `rollout status`.
questions.solution:
# The container declares no resources, so compute-quota refuses it.
kubectl -n ckad-quotas patch deployment shipit --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources","value":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"64Mi"},"limits":{"cpu":"200m","memory":"128Mi"}}}]'
kubectl -n ckad-quotas rollout status deployment/shipit

verification.description: Deployment shipit has >=1 available replica (quota-rejection fixed in the pod template)
